title: Synthesize optimal weighted reversible binary words with full endpoint replay
body:
Add a bounded constructor for optimal reversible binary linear words with custom XOR/SWAP alphabets and positive integer prices. It searches the full generated finite group, emits a complete potential/closure certificate, and replays the attaining word literally on every input. A closed set excluding the target proves unreachability in the declared alphabet.

Six tests pass normally and under -O on CPython 3.12.14. Every one of the 168 three-role endpoints agrees with an independent truth-table shortest-path oracle. The four-role case covers all 20160 invertible maps and certifies six XORs for full reversal. Tests also cover a cheaper XOR implementation of an expensive SWAP, restricted alphabets, singular targets, false words/potentials and portable source-hash replay.

Credit classical finite-group search and the existing zero-frame feedback censuses, whose larger six/eight-role unit-cost source contracts remain separate. Limits: four arbitrary roles, 18 distinct generators and costs in 1..10^9. No clean ancillas, hidden basis permutations, frame changes or free restoration are introduced. Native phases, tensor semantics and complete caller prices require their own checks. Minimum scalar cost is not a kappa result.

Fresh main/priorities/overlap checked at both checkpoints. Canonical scope https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5776. No frontier change. All 6 new tests pass in the [hosted plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40382197440/job/121781082472) at this head. The plan fails on the unchanged assignment module (8 failures and 2 errors); replay is skipped. The existing fix is [PR #5761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5761). Independent review remains pending.

Base: `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. Verified head: `9ddb022cc1d879a5d3173f8f1f526a2ff504e7b3`.

Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retained tool and mathematical predecessor credits apply. No selected-frontier change.
